prompt: Compare these two contracts on termination, liability and renewal: the Atlas Logistics MSA and the Borealis Freight MSA.

assistant_messages.content:
Atlas has the longer notice periods and more balanced terms. Borealis can be ended on short notice, its liability terms are one-sided, and it says nothing about renewal. That last point matters now: going by the dates in the contract, the Borealis term appears to have already run out.

| | **Atlas Logistics MSA** (signed 14 Mar 2023) | **Borealis Freight MSA** (effective 1 Jun 2024) |
|---|---|---|
| **Ending it at will** | Either party can end it with 90 days' written notice [1] | Either party can end it with 30 days' written notice [2] |
| **Ending it for a problem** | Either party can end it at once for a serious breach that isn't fixed within 30 days of written notice [1] | Only the Company can end it, at once, and only if Borealis becomes insolvent. There's no general breach clause [2] |
| **Liability cap** | Same for both sides: the fees paid in the 12 months before the claim [1] | Different for each side. Borealis: €250,000 per year. The Company: the fees payable in that year [2] |
| **What the cap doesn't cover** | Death, personal injury, fraud and breach of confidentiality [1] | Fraud only [2] |
| **Term and renewal** | Renews automatically for one year at a time unless either side gives written notice at least 90 days before the term ends [1] | Fixed two-year term with no renewal clause [2] |
| **Price changes** | Prices rose 3.5% in Amendment 1 (Feb 2024) and 3.1% in April 2026, "within the 4 percent cap" [1] | Not covered |

**Termination:** Atlas gives both sides more protection: three months' notice, and a 30-day chance to fix a breach before either side can walk away. Borealis can be ended by either side in a month. It also doesn't let the Company end it for poor performance short of insolvency, so you'd have to use the 30-day at-will exit instead.

**Liability:** The Atlas cap works the same both ways and has the usual four exclusions. With Borealis, if the fees you pay in a year are less than €250,000, Borealis is capped higher than you are. Borealis's only exclusion is fraud. That means claims for personal injury or breach of confidentiality would still be capped, and the document doesn't contain a confidentiality clause at all.

**Renewal — two dates to act on:**
- **Atlas:** The current term ends on 15 March 2027, so the last day to give notice of non-renewal is **15 December 2026**, about 7 weeks away [1]. If no notice is given, it renews for another year.
- **Borealis:** A two-year term starting 1 June 2024 would have ended around 31 May 2026 [2]. That's my own calculation; the document doesn't give an end date. Nothing in it provides for renewal, so unless there's an extension stored somewhere else, the contract may have lapsed. If you're still using Borealis, it would be worth checking what terms you're actually working under.

Neither document states governing law, indemnities or what happens after termination. Both are also marked as generated test documents with no real parties or amounts.
